1. Pet 2. 9 -- a Peculiar People ------ [^006-note18] This we shall not much Insist upon inasmuch as many things that might have been said upon it have been said already under the former heads. But shall briefly show how they are Gods Peculiar People in the following Respects 1 True Xtians are Gods Peculiar. ---- People with Respect to the value God sest sets upon them for he sets a hi in that he sets a higher value upon one true Xtian than upon all the wicked in the T . God sets a high value upon his saints they are his Jewels as they are Called. Gods high value of them appears in all the ways wherin persons are wont to show their Poss a Great value that they set upon any possesssion G. Keeps them as the apple of his Eye he will by no means Loose one of his saints not not one of all the numb. shall fail he by no means will suffer any to do them harm his almighty Power & Inf is thoroughly Engaged for them to defend them . The Great value that G. sets upon them appears by the Great Price that G. was at to Purchase them G. sets a high the Life the happiness & welfare of the saints is precious in Gods sight. that God values one saint more than all the Ungodly in th [them] thousands of ungodly men Yea more than all the ungodly in the T. God shows the higher value that he sets upon ther Godly than others by Giving the wicked for them destroyi making them subservient to them & destroying them when they stands in the Godly way of the welfare of the Godly. Prov 21 . 18 . the wicked shall be a Ransom for the Righteous and the transgressour for the upright. [^006-note19] this is to show how much more highly G. values the Righteous than the wicked as if a man had a Child in the hand of an Enemy and should be willing to Give a hundred slaves to Redeem that one Child this would show that he set a higher value upon that Child than upon all those slaves. so G. whenever the wickeds life or welfare of the wicked stands in the way of the welfare of the Righteous G. is wont to Procure the welfare of his people tho it be to at the expence of never so man the lives or welfares of never so many of them. so Prov. 11. 8 the Righteous is delivered out of Trouble and the wicked Cometh in his stead. Thus God sets forth his C the value that he set upon Abra the Patriarchs tho there were but very few of them yet Even Kings were Rebuked for their sakes Ps 105. 12. when they were but a few men in number yea very few and strangers in it when they went from one nation to another from one Kingd. to another Peop. he suffered no man to do them wrong Yea he Reproved Kings for their sakes. saying Touch not mine Anointed and do my Prophets no harm. so he sets forth the value th he sets upon the Chil. of Israel who by that that he Gave nations for them Isai 43. 3. 4. for I am the L. thy G. the Holy one of Is. thy sav. I C Gave Egypt for thy Ransom Ethiopia & sheba for thee. since thou wast Precious in my sight thou hast been honourable & I have loved thee therefore will I Give men for thee & People for thy life.

## 195. Ps. 108:4 195.Ps. 108'4 trans

Jonathan Edwards

Ps. 108.4. For thy mercy is Great Above the Heavens.

_________________________

By this Expression the of the Psalmist the Riches & Glory of the divine mercy is Elegantly set forth The Psalmist from the Contemplation of those the Acts of mercy which Gods Gracious acts which were the occasion of this song of Praise had Concieved a most Exalted thought of that attribute. divine Attribute. which naturally excited expressed it self in such a metaphor as this that it is Great above the H.

_______________________

This metaphor very naturally siginifies in the General an a superlative inexpressible & Incomprehensible Greatness of & Excellency of the mercy of G. the expanse of the the Expanse of the Heavens is the Greatest & most Extensive thing that we have in view or that may we have any notice of by our senses of & the height thereof is Immen Immesurable & Inconcievable Job 11 . 8 . tis high as heaven what Canst thou do.

_______________________

hereby is well denoted the vastly excess of Gods mercy exalwher me G. exceeds all other beings in mercy or how Great his mercy is above that of all other when Compared with Creature mercy the heaven heavens are hi vastly higher than all things here upon Earth and G. in this Respect is above us as high as the heavens are high above the Earth as tis said of Gods ways & our wor & thoughts & mens when by the prophet when speaking of this attribute . Isai 55 9 .

__________

stones and Pearls sitting on a scarlet Coloured beast full of names of blasphemy having seven heads & ten horns .

we have here an account that Remarkeable account of Jacobs Wrestling with G. it was at a time when Jacob was Expecting to meet his Brother Esau . who was now Coming out with four hundred Armed men upon a hostile design against him. Jacob had divided his Company & sent them over before he the ford Jabbok but he himself stai & put em into that order in which he would have em meet their Esau & send them away over the ford Jabbok .but he himself staid Brook in the night but he himself staid behind em alone Probably it was that he might have the better opportunity by to Prevent to seek Gods favour & s to Pour out his supplications to G. & seek his favour at this Junctre & mercy at this Juncture In when they were so Eminently threatend with destruction from Esau & his Company

& while he was there alone in the night there Came a man to him as he in as one in a human form & with an human body . the son it seems to have been the son of G. the scond Person in the Trinity that appeared to him the son of G. who had undert his delight undertaken to be mans Mediatour & Representative surety and was to take on him the human nature was wont frequently under the old Testament to appear in human shape. . and sometimes assumed a hu or probably sometimes assumed an human body occasionally assumed an human body as he did before his Proper [^014-note1] Incarnation as he did when he at & drank with Abraham in the Plains of mamre. & as he did now when he wrestled with Jacob . whenever G. appeared under the old Testament it is probable it was the second Person by of the Godhead . by what X says is said Joh 1 . 18 no man hath seen G. at any time; the only begotten son who which is in the Bosom of the Father he hath declared him . we have an account that this he that Came to Jab Jacob wrestled with him all the Remainder of the night

________________

It seems that Jacob did not Know that it was G. till the Last . But doubtless Immediately Percieved that he some very Extraordinary Person Eminently in wisd. & holiness by his appearance tho it was in the night & also. by his Conversation that he was some very Extraordinary Person Eminently wise & holy & might they think him to be an Angel. . for perh Jacob had not been altogether unused to such a thing as Angels appearing to him . for he had had a vision of Angels at Bethel and an the Angels of G. met him again at mahanaim before this . Jacob did not only wrestle with him in a figurative sense as the saints may be said to wrestle with G. in Prayer. but he wrestled with him Literally . tho he did not Know then that it was G. .

__________________________

I will not Presume to determine how Jacob Came to wrestle with him & what was the Occasion of Jacobs wres wrestling with him or how they Came to be Engaged in such Exercise but I will venture to Inform you what appears to [^014-note2] be me to be Probable . viz. That he that appeard to Ja the man that appeared Came to Jacob. or that appeard to him as a man had been in a free & familiar had been in a most free & Condescending & friendly manner Conversing with Jacob . so that Jacob & and he appearg to Jacob in his Conversation with him so Excellent holy & wise & Excellent a Person & amiable a Person & had Conversed with him in so Friendly Condescending & Friendly a manner . that Jacob was Greatly delighted with his Company . & upon his making as tho he would Go away Jacob Could being very Loth to Part with him might Layd hold of him to stay him that he might have more of his Company . & Hence Emb followed a wrestle between them the divine Person & the man that appeared striving as tho he would Get away & Jacob to hold him Back . hence followed a wrestling between em . Jacob might was Embolden'd to such freedom by the Extraordinary meekness . Goodness & friendliness of his Conver of his Conversation with him . & so it is said they wrestled till break of day . the Person then more Insisted. upon to appears more Resolute to depart & says to Jacob Let me Go for the day breaketh . Jacob Replies I will not Let thee Go except thou bless me. Jacob was Resolved upon this that if he Could be would depart & he Could have no more of his Company Yet he would if Possible obtain his blessing before he that Extraordinary Excellency & wisd that & holiness [^014-note3] that appeard in him made him value his blessing. But still Jacob did not Know that it was God .

These are the first words that G. spoke to the moses or the Chi Chil. of Is. after they Came to mt sinai. G. had spoken to moses from mt sinai before bu alone from mt sinai before & that was when he Kept the flock of his Father in Law and appeared to him in the Burning Bush & bid him Loose his shoe from off his foot because the Place where he stood was holy Ground that was that we have an Account of in the 3 Chap. of this B. Gods Great Care of their safety in his Providences towards them & how I Bare you on Eagles wings that is on high & far a above the Reach of your Enemies or any thing that might hurt th You An Eagle is a Bird very Lofty in her flight and when soars as she flies aloft she Goes where she desires & is out of the Reach of all that are here below those are below we Cant Reach here to hurt her or to turn her Interrupt her in her Progress. so G. Carried the Chil . of Israel Israelas it were on high in the Air aloft aloft in the Air where their Enemies Could not Reach em to Annoy em they Could see Em & Could wish ill to em but all that they Could do they Could not Reach em to hurt them or to hinder their Going where G . would Go Carry them & G. 2 . we may Observe and whe the thing wherein That is here Predicated of man. That Zophar takes notice of wherein man shows his pride viz that he would be wise. i. e he is Ready to Conceit himself wise or is Ready to Grasp as Great wisd. than Reach after & Grasp at Greater wisd than he is able to attain to . man has a proud vain affectation of bieng wiser & wiser than he is or Can be beyond his Line This appeard in mans first sin ------

3 we may Observe wherein the vanity & absurdity. of his affecting to be wise appears viz that he is born like a wild asses Colt . It was the design of Prov. in ordering man to Come into the Θ Like the brute Creatures to teach us our Infirmity & weakness & Impotency & our being Clothed with flesh as they are our being of the dust like them should Keep us from affecting to be like G. and aspiring Proudly after Greater Proudly aspiring . a R man after high things [-] Remembring that we are of the dust . & ashes [^018-note2] and born Like the wild asses Colt should be Enough to Humble us doc . That man is naturally a Proud Creature. [rest of L. 2r. blank] [L. 2v. blank] Prov. 29. 23. a mans Pride shall bring him Low .

## 210. Prov. 16:4 210.Prov. 16'4 trans

Jonathan Edwards

Prov . 16 4 . The L. hath made all things for himself yea Even the wicked for the day of Evil.

__________________________________

In the Text we Have a Proposition first Generally Laid down & then Particularly applied . 1 here is a Proposition Generally Laid down . The L. hath made all things for himself . Here is Included first G what G hath done he hadth made all things. By all things here are are not only meant all the works of Creation for the wicked as wicked are no part of the work of Creation G. never Created any wicked man or wicked being all the works of Creation were very Good . but by all things here is plainly meant all things that are brought to Pass in the universe Including th all the works of Creation and whatsoever Comes to Pass in Provid. that the wickedness of man is one thing that which Comes to Pass in Provid . the word made in the Text is not to be taken of any Positive efficience. but that G. hath Ordered & disposed all things Positive things & things beings & things that are Good he hath made by a Proper Efficiency & others he [-] hath ordained and they Come to Pass through his Permission . .

_____________________________________

& then in this Prop. is decla 2 . in this Proposition is declared the End of this work G. herein he hath made all things for Himself whatsoever is and what soever Comes to Pass . all things that appear in heaven & Earth & all things little and Great & that Ever Came to Pass in Prov. G. hath Ordained & disposed for him self they Come to Pass for Gods Gods Ends an for Ends that he Proposes for An End that he Proposes & himself [^024-note1] is that End It becomes G. to make himself his End . it becomes him to Propose the most Noble & excellent End but he Can Propose no more higher End than himself whenever we look abroad & see the various Objects that appear in the visible T we may Consider that all these things hath G. made for himself. & whatever we see or hear of that Comes to pass in Provid. here or Elsewhere we may Consider that these things dont Come to Pass accidentally but G. hath Ordered them for himself . But then how doth G. order order all things for himself who needs nothing & Can Recieve nothing Can have no addition of any Proper benefit or happiness by any thing that is made . But we are told Else where how G. makes things for himself Isai 43. 7. I have Created him for my Glory I have formed him yea I have made him G. saw it a Conducent & meet thing that he should Glory Glorify himself tho he stand in need of no happiness & for thin this End hath he made all things. 2 This universal Proposition is Proposition is Particularly applied to the wicked or to their being are Part of Gods work of Creation as to their wickedness they belong to & then keeps the wicked to the day of Evil . Here first that the wise man observes that Even they are Some of them those that G. has made for himself . the wicked as to their Being are some of Gods works of Creation . and as to their wickedness they belong to Gods Permissive [^024-note2] Provid . the wise man says that Even these G hath G. made for himself he applies the General Prop. to that man he foresaw man would be Ready to Except here is the Greatest difficulty both in supposing that the wickedness of man is of Gods decree appointment . and also in supposing that it is for Gods Comes to Pass for divine Ends . but yet this also is not Excepted G. hath both hath made even the wicked for himself . But then 2dly 2dly the wise man shows how as by what means G. will obtain his End of in them & that it in they their Evil & the wicked for the day of Evil the End of the beings of wicked men is obtained in their d Just the misery their misery.

## 218. Jer. 6:4 218.Jer. 6'4 trans

Jonathan Edwards

Jer 6. 4. wo unto us the day Goeth Away the shadows of the Evening are stretched out.

_________________

These are the words of the Enemies of Jerusalem the work that G. had set them about was to destroy Jerusalem . Jerusalem is Liken'd to a tender & delicate woman And the hers Enemies to shepherds with their flocks that shall Come and Pitch their Tents Round about her & besiege her . these Express their Ear n Engagedness in their work of destroying Her. by Lamenting the Lateness shortness of the time they have to do it in we may here Observe 1. the thing they Lament the day Goeth Away wh i.e the Greater Part of the day is Gone and time is still Continually Passing & the short Remainder will be all Soon Gone. 2. what is the sign of this which they take notice of & that is that the shadows of the Evening are stretched out . this is a sign of declining day & approaching night that they Observed the Evening shadows were stretched out. This as the day Goes away Evening approaches the shadows of things Grow Long are stretched out to Length to a Great Length.

________________________________________________________

Doc. Tis very sorrowfull when tis Late in the day with Persons and a P work of Great Importance & difficulty Remains undone that must be done before the Day be Past.

________________________________________________________________________

Tis so with Respect to any work or Business in proportion to the Importance and difficulty of it or according to the necessity there is of the Works being [^032-note1] done and according to the difficulty there is in doing of it or the Greatness and difficulty of the Work or the time which will necessarily be taken up in doing of it.

____________________________________

But what we I aim at Particularly is that Great work that G. has G of securing an interest in X which G. has Given us to do in the day of our Lives . & therefore I would show 1. There there is a Great work that G. hath of Great Importance & difficulty which G. has Given us to do. 2. That tis a work that must be done in the day of Life. 3. Therefore tis sorrowfull.

____________________________________________________________

I. There is a Great W. of Great Importance & difficulty which G. has Given us all to do . It be Properly belongs to Who him Who made us to appoint us our Work and business in the T and there is a work that our maker has appointed us G. has not made us for Nothing he has not furnished with Reason & wit such superior faculties & Capacities of action and with so many talents means or Instruments to work with & Yet Given us no work to do in the T . the work that G. Created us for was to serve & Glorify him & in that way to obtain our own happiness & now we are in a fallen state the work that we have appointed us is to Return to G. from whom we are fallen to Get Recovered from our fallen Condition & Get Reconciled unto G. to Get our natures Renewed. & sanctified to forsake sin & turn to G. by J. X in sincerity & Truth. or in one word to Obtain a time that through him we [^032-note2] may be again Reconciled to G. & may Obtain the favour and aceptance of G. that we have Lost by our defection . or in short our Great work is to obtain and make sure of a thorough sound and thorough Conversion to G. & Interest in his favour.

_________________________________________

This is a Great work. in two Respects. viz Great Importance. Great Difficulty.

___________________________________________________________

1. Tis a W. of Great Importance. tis a work of the Greatest Conceivable Importance tis Impossible to Express the Importance of this Work. a matter of Infinite Concern depends upon it a viz the salv. of our souls . tis of such Imp. that if it be not done it will expose us to an Infinite Calamity we must necessarily unavoidably Perish forever we must be miserable to all Eternity and if and if it be done it will Redound to our Everlasting happiness & felicita & Glory so that the work is of Infinite Import. upon a double account as the Import. of it is doubly Infinite tis Infin. as tis of absolute necessity to to deliveranc us from a Calamity that is Infinite & again the Import of it is infinite because our obtaining or not obtaining an Infinite felicity depends upon it. there is no other work is of Import. in any wise as this is our Interest in small Inconsiderable Instances may depend upon other things our temporal Interest may depend upon it we ma by neglecting we may expose our selves to Great temporal Calamities & by doing may make sure of Considerable temporal advantages[^032-note3] but the Greatest temporal advantages or disadvantages that we Can be the subjects of it are not to Compared to those that are Eternal. tho they may seem Great in themselves yet when we Come to Compare em with what Eternal happiness or mis. they are as nothing and not worthy of any Regard temporal things Let em be never so Great bear no Greater Proportion to Eternal than nothing to something

_______________________________

Therefore this Work may be looked upon as being the only Great and Important work that we have to do for for our whole Interest & Happiness depend upon it our all depends upon it if this bent done we are Ruin'd forever & if it be done we are made forever. if a man has Eternal happi ness secured to him what Need he Care how his Inferior Interests Go . Eternal Happiness is all Enough & Eternal happiness is Enough Who Can desire to have more than Eternal happiness.

so that we see that this work that G. has Given man to do is the only Important work that he has [^032-note4] to do because his all depends upon it.

2 As it is a w. of Great Importance so tis a w. of Great diffic. as it ordinarily is those works or Businesses that are of Great Importance that will be of Great Advantage to us are Attended with Special difficul ties. so hath Providence ordered and it is wisely ordered tis fitting those that those things That are peculiarly excellent & Contain them any very Great advantage should be attended with more difficulty than others. for tis Re for a trial of of our value & Esteem of them and of an that none May Obtain them but those that are in some Good measure sensible of the worth of them and have the Prudence as to undergo the Labour be willing to undergo Labour & difficulty for them

This & Great work that we are speaking of that is of such Infinite Importance is attended with many & Great difficulties. It is ordinarily a wor tho the work be not a work that is wrou Properly depends on our strength or Endeavours Yet it is ordinarily a work that Requires a Great deal of our Labour & diligence in order to its being done & it Requires the Laying out of our utmost strength it Requires a Great deal of Constancy[^032-note5] & Perseverance steadiness. without wavering or discouragemt a work the Requires a Great deal of application of thought a Great deal of Care & watchfullness & abundance of strictness & exactness in our behaviour . tis a work that Requires a Great deal of Engagedness in our affections & a Great deal of Resolution Tis a work wherein we stand in a need of a Great Inst deal of direction & Counsel Least we miss our way or should Labour in vain. Tis a work that is attended with many dangers in the there are many things that do attend it that tend to frustrates all persons Endeavours & Labours in attempting to do it and to make all that they do or have done to. in vain and to no purpose. There is danger of Erring in it is a work in attempting of which many have Come short and many have been Confounded and Lost & suffered shipwreck wreck . Tis a work that is attended with a Great deal of opposition there are many Enemies that oppose us in doing of it that are Continually Endeavouring to weaken our hands to block up our way to divert us & hinder us & make our work more difficult by all ways that they Can devise

## 219. Jer. 10:16 219.Jer. 10'16 trans

Jonathan Edwards

+ + Nov. 57. Jer. 10. 16. The Portion of Jacob is not Like them & Israel is for he is the former of all things and Israel is the Rod of his Inheritance the L. of hosts is his name . The Prophet in this Chap is speaking of the Idols of the Heathen & setting forth their vanity. and tis they that are spoken of when it is said here that the portion of Jacob is not Like them . The difference between the True G. & Idols is here set forth in three things . 1 in his works. he is the former of all things . The True G.mak makes under the Whole universe and all Heaven & Ear This is a Remarkeable difference as for those Idols Instead of being formers of all things they were not the formers of all things They did not make those Heavens and this Earth v. 11. It Instead of being the formers of all things they themselves are formed by mens hands as in the 3d fourth and 5v. one Cutteth a Tree out of the Forest. & 9. v. silver spread into Plates is brought .

_______________________________

The second difference but here Observed between the True G. & Idold Idols is in the Relation that he stands in to Israel. & this is twofold first that God is their Portion & 2 secondly that G is t they are his portion . he is the portion of Jacob. & Israel is the Rod of his Inheritance. By Jab Jacob & Israel are to be Understood of not only the The nation of Israel. but mo Chiefly the spiritual [^033-note1] Israel . these are often not only the the Xtians The Godly of all nations these are often times Called Israel God is their portion the other Gods G. had divided deut 4.19

## 225. Zech. 7:5-6 225.Zech. 7'5-6 trans

Jonathan Edwards

Zech. 7. 5, 6. speak unto all the People of the Land and to the Priests saying when ye fasted and mourned in the fifth & seventh month Even those seventy Years did ye at all fast unto me Even to me? and when ye did Eat and when ye did drink did ye not Eat for your selves and drink for your selves

______________________________________

Zechariah was one of those Prophets that G Raised up after the Captivity. we G. Raised up these two Prophets Haggai & Zechariah upon the Return of the Jews from their Captivity to Encourage the Jews in their build Res Rebuilding Jerusalem & the Temple & Resettling the Land . we Read of them in Ezra 5. 1. v. then the Prophets Haggai the Proph. & Zech. the son of Iddo Prophesied unto the Jews that were in Judah & Jerusalem in the name of the G. of Is. Even unto them.

_________________________

There were was but three Prophets Raised up in Israel after the Captivity viz Hag. Z. & Mal. untill X after them the sp. of Proph. Ceased till the Gr In Israel untill the Great Prophet . so that that nation were for near 400 years without any Prophet appearing among them.

________________________

In order the understanding that Passage of ss that has been now Read the Prophecy of Zech . that has been now Read it must be Observed that the Chil of I Jews during their seventy Years Captivity had been wont to Keep a fast on the fifth and anothe Every year on the fifth and another in the seventh month . in that fast in the fifth month was in Remembrance of [^038-note1] the destruction of Jerusalem in Zedekiahs time which was in this month as you may see Jer. 52. 12. 13. &c-----

______________________________________________________________

-----------and the Jews yearly Kept a fast at the same time of time of year to Lament & bewail this destruction

_______________________________________

& they Kept another fast on in the seventh month which seems to have been in Remembrance of the destruction of Gedaliah & the Remnant of the Jews in mizpah by Ismael the son of nethaniah . of which we Read in the 2d of Kings 25. 25. zeb But it Came to Pass in the seventh month that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah the son of Elishama of the seed Royal Came and ten men with him & smote Gedaliah that he died and the Jews & the Chaldees that were with him at Mizpah The Kept a Yearly fast to bew Remember & bewail this also.

___________

These fasts were not Instituted by any Prophet but were of their own Invention they thought it that being that such dreadfull Calamities happened at these times it was but suitable to Keep a fast Every Year at Least while they Continued in Captivity in Remembrance thereof, and having Agreed to it used them Agreed to it & accustomed themselves to it from Year to Year they Came to make as much Conscience of it as of Keeping those holy days that were of divine Institution.

_____________________

But now the Jews being many of them Returned from the Captivity and having Re begun to build Jerusalem & the Temple Again. & those sorrowfull times that were Introduced [^038-note2] by those Calamities that the fasts w their fasts were Kept in Remembrance of being in a measure at an End [-] there began a question to Arise among them Whether or no they ought among those of the Jews that Continued Yet in Babi Chaldea & wh Babilon whether or no they ought to Keep these fasts any Longer. & to have their question Resolved they sent. & sent two messengers sherezer & Regemmelech up to Jerusalem to the House of G. & to the Prophets in Jerusalem to be Resolved in this question. 2 & 3 v.----------------------------------

## 226. Zech. 8:23 226.Zech. 8'23 trans

Jonathan Edwards

This sermon shows signs of revision by Edwards, by Grosart (who signed it on leaf 19 recto), and by a third editor who struck out certain words to make (mostly stylistic) changes. Grosart's revision may be found on leaf 3 verso; the other changes have been noted in brackets in the margin, and are indicated by quotation marks around those words which are crossed out in ink different from Edwards's. Zech 8 . 23. Thus saith the L. of Hosts in those days it shall Come to Pass that ten men shall take hold out of all Languages of the Nations Even shall take hold of the skirt of him that is a Jew saying we will Go with You for we have heard that G . is with you . 23 . 21 77 .

__________________

This and the foregoing Chap. is the W. of the L. that Came to the Prophet upon the Occasion of the messengers sherezer & Regemm . Coming from the Jews that were Yet in Babilon to Jerusalem with a Case of Consc. viz whether or no they should Yet uphold those fasts that had hither to been Kept in Commemoration Commemoration of the destructio the destruction of Judea & Jerusalem . they had in Babilon during the Captivi ty Kept several fasts at different times of Year In those times of the year wherein the most mem memorable Ca disasters Befell them that Contributing Contributed to the destruction of their state as the fast of the fourth month when the City was broken up & the Chaldeans took Zedekiah and all the Princes of the Land & the fast of the fifth month when the King of Babilon Burnt the City of Jerusalem Temple & City of Jerusalem & the fast of the seventh month when Ishmael the son of nethaniah slew Gedaliah & the Jews of mizpah & of the Tenth month when the nebuchadnezzar Came & besieged the Cit Jerusalem . the Prophet Answers those messengers By Reproving of them the Jews them their By Reproving them their hypocrisy & formality in [-] Keeping & setting so much by such observances & neglecting [L. 1v.] In the mean while the Commands of the moral Law that are of Greater weight & Importance . The Prophet therefore Exhorting them to the Rev Practice of moral duties Instead of Placing so much Religion in those fasts such observances the more necessary & substantial duties of Religion Instead of Plai Placing so much Relig . in Fasting such Fasts .
